papers.title: Specialeafhandling: Scaling AI in Organisations: An Empirical Study of Organisational Conditions Differentiating Enterprise Adoption from the Pilot Trap

summary.goal: The study examines organisational conditions that enable enterprises to scale AI beyond isolated pilot projects.
summary.methodology: It uses a sociotechnical and dynamic-capabilities perspective based on six semi-structured interviews with external consultants across industries.
summary.finding: Successful scaling depends on organisational alignment, governance, strategic anchoring, collaboration, user adoption, workflow integration, and adaptive, absorptive, and innovative capabilities, while fragmented ownership, skill gaps, and compliance barriers contribute to the pilot trap.

papers.title: The Ethical and Legal Complexities of Regulating Companion AI Chatbots
papers.authors: Sue Anne Teo, S. P. Mann, Paul Jurcys

summary.goal: The article examines the ethical and legal challenges posed by companion AI chatbots and develops a theory of harm for digitally mediated intimacy.
summary.methodology: It analyzes companion AI through anthropomorphism, emotional AI, emergent vulnerabilities, and mismatched legal taxonomies.
summary.finding: The article argues that existing frameworks inadequately address companion AI harms and proposes intimacy capitalism as a framework for analyzing the monetization and exploitation of digitally mediated intimate relations.

papers.title: “Noticed but not used”: The gap between AI feedback and its delayed application in L2 academic writing
papers.authors: Akihiko Sasaki Akihiko Sasaki, Osamu Takeuchi
papers.journal: Asian Journal of English Language Teaching

summary.goal: The study investigates which linguistic forms university students notice through ChatGPT feedback in L2 academic writing and whether they subsequently apply them.
summary.methodology: It qualitatively analyzes student interviews, ChatGPT history logs, and draft revisions.
summary.finding: Students noticed diverse vocabulary and syntactic structures, but cognitive load, fear of mistakes, and task-completion pressure limited their independent use.

papers.title: When language feels like recognition: Parasocial Mattering Resonance as a cognitive vulnerability in human–LLM interaction

summary.goal: The paper develops the concept of Parasocial Mattering Resonance to explain how LLM language may produce experiences of recognition and mattering among individuals with unmet relational needs.
summary.methodology: It uses schema accessibility theory, dual-process models of social cognition, and a five-dimension mattering framework to propose a mechanism and six formal propositions.
summary.finding: The paper argues that PMR may increase compliance, reduce skepticism, extend engagement, and displace human relationships, with vulnerability concentrated among marginalized and isolated individuals.

papers.title: When Intelligence Becomes Exposure: The Cybersecurity Implications of Organizational LLM
papers.authors: Issack Shama Guyo, Stefan A Mills, Nan Xiao
papers.journal: Journal of the Association for Information Systems

summary.goal: The study examines how organizational reliance on LLM-generated outputs may reduce employees’ cybersecurity vigilance and increase vulnerability.
summary.methodology: It develops a conceptual argument drawing on Sociotechnical Systems Theory and research on automation bias.
summary.finding: The abstract argues that cognitive delegation to LLMs can weaken verification behavior, with effects shaped by AI literacy, cybersecurity culture, and human review mechanisms.

papers.title: When Health Is at Stake: Comparing User Perceptions of Generative AI Chatbots for Chronic Disease Information Seeking
papers.journal: Journal of the Association for Information Systems

summary.goal: The study examines how perceived information and interaction quality influence trust, continued use, and behavioral intentions when people use generative AI chatbots for chronic disease information seeking.
summary.methodology: It uses a scenario-based online experiment in which participants interact with one of four assigned chatbots: ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, or DeepSeek.
summary.finding: The abstract does not report findings.

papers.title: When AI speaks: user imaginaries of generative AI and freedom of expression

summary.goal: The study examines how active generative AI users understand the technology’s effects on freedom of expression, authorship, visibility, and public debate.
summary.methodology: Researchers conducted in-depth interviews with active GenAI users on X and analyzed them thematically using the concept of GenAI imaginaries.
summary.finding: Participants identified five imaginaries—Pragmatic Tool, Knowledge Authority, Hybrid Speech, Power Struggle, and Ethical Issues—highlighting concerns about guardrails, misinformation, authorship, autonomy, and accountability.

papers.title: What do we know about generative AI and learning?
papers.authors: Nancy Butler Songer, C.M. Logan, Niral Shah, David Stroupe

summary.goal: The paper discusses what is known about generative AI and its impact on learning.
summary.methodology: The abstract presents a conceptual discussion of generative AI, its development, and its capabilities.
summary.finding: The abstract does not report findings.

papers.title: Voxvoro: Repurposing Social Media UI Patterns for AI-Augmented Scholarly Synthesis
papers.journal: Journal of the Association for Information Systems

summary.goal: The project aims to reduce scholarly information overload by using a local LLM to transform academic metadata into structured concept cards and audio summaries.
summary.methodology: It describes a mobile PWA that retrieves scholarly works through OpenAlex, summarizes them with Gemma3:27b, generates audio with a text-to-speech model, and evaluates the artifact with university faculty using self-reported engagement data and qualitative feedback.
summary.finding: The abstract does not report findings.

papers.title: Vietnamese EFL Students’ Perceptions and Preferences for ChatGPT, Peer, and Teacher Feedback in Writing Revision<b></b>
papers.authors: Thi Diep Nguyen, Xuan Quan Nguyen

summary.goal: The study examined Vietnamese university EFL students’ perceptions and preferences regarding ChatGPT, peer, and teacher feedback during writing revision.
summary.methodology: It used an explanatory sequential mixed-methods design with questionnaires from 110 English majors and semi-structured interviews with 10 selected participants.
summary.finding: Students rated teacher feedback highest, valued ChatGPT for immediacy, and generally supported combining all three feedback sources with explicit training.

papers.title: Uso de la inteligencia artificial en el desarrollo del pensamiento crítico en estudiantes de bachillerato.
papers.authors: María Paz Mancheno-Oviedo, Santiago David Yanzapanta-Garcés, Genesis Dayana Pinto Almeida, Jacqueline Estefania Rodríguez-Loor

summary.goal: Analizar la influencia del uso de ChatGPT en el desarrollo del pensamiento crítico de estudiantes de bachillerato.
summary.methodology: Se aplicó un enfoque cuantitativo descriptivo no experimental mediante una encuesta estructurada a 182 estudiantes.
summary.finding: El 60% usa ChatGPT frecuentemente, principalmente para generar ideas y comprender contenidos, sin evidenciarse una disminución significativa del pensamiento crítico, cuyo desarrollo depende del tipo de uso.

papers.title: University students’ AI attitudes: an experiential transformation
papers.authors: Aydın Çivilidağ, Yiğit Dora, Şüheda Erbay, Şaduman Şimşek, Şerife Durmaz

summary.goal: The study examines how direct interaction with ChatGPT-4o changes university students’ perceptions of AI and career-related attitudes.
summary.methodology: Eighteen university students participated in a two-stage qualitative study involving metaphor elicitation before and after a structured chess interaction with ChatGPT-4o.
summary.finding: Students shifted from idealized perceptions of AI to more critical evaluations after observing its strategic limitations and inconsistencies.

papers.title: Understanding the Influence of Agentic AI on Workplace Dignity
papers.journal: Journal of the Association for Information Systems

summary.goal: The study examines how varying levels of Agentic AI automation influence workers’ perceptions of workplace dignity.
summary.methodology: It uses a field experiment that randomly presents participants with task designs involving different levels of AI autonomy.
summary.finding: The abstract does not report findings.

papers.title: Uncovering Bias: Leveraging Large Language Models for News Analysis inthe Context of Palestine

summary.goal: The study aims to detect and understand media bias in news coverage of the Israel-Palestine conflict using sentiment as a proxy for emotional framing.
summary.methodology: It analyzes 9,000 labeled news articles and compares DistilBERT, BERT-Mini, TinyBERT, GRU, RNN, and LSTM models.
summary.finding: Transformer-based models outperform sequential models, with DistilBERT achieving the best performance at 94% accuracy.

papers.title: Trust-driven consensus reaching in human-AI hybrid large-scale group decision-making
papers.authors: Xinyu Wang, Xuanhua Xu, Weiwei Zhang

summary.goal: The paper aims to improve trust representation, conflict feedback, and consensus efficiency in human–AI group decision-making.
summary.methodology: It models dynamic trust relationships between human experts and large language models, uses trust-based opinion updating, and iteratively regulates consensus using the Zhengzhou “7.20” rainstorm case.
summary.finding: The abstract reports that the method preliminarily achieves higher consensus quality with lower intervention costs than traditional weight adjustment and deep-reinforcement-learning regulation methods.

papers.title: Towards a methodologically congruent framework for GenAI use in nonpositivist qualitative research
papers.journal: International Journal of Social Research Methodology

summary.goal: The article develops a methodologically congruent framework for using GenAI in nonpositivist qualitative research.
summary.methodology: It distinguishes technological and qualitative methodological incongruence and proposes using GenAI as an interlocutor through relational, ethical, researcher-led, and abductive practices.
summary.finding: GenAI can support surfacing, retrieving, comparing, and suggesting qualitative material, but human researchers remain responsible for interpretation and meaning-making.

papers.title: The serial mediating effects of learning motivation and learning engagement on the relationship between gen AI literacy and EFL perceived proficiency among vocational students
papers.authors: Rui Zhang, Othman Bin Talib, Shengnan Liu, Zhixinlu Chen, Daliang Lu, Yufang Meng

summary.goal: The study examines whether learning motivation and engagement serially mediate the relationship between generative AI literacy and vocational students’ perceived EFL proficiency.
summary.methodology: It uses a cross-sectional survey of 383 vocational college students in China with validated measures of Gen AI literacy, motivation, engagement, and perceived EFL proficiency.
summary.finding: Gen AI literacy positively predicted perceived proficiency and motivation, with a significant serial mediation pathway through motivation and engagement.

papers.title: The quasi-gods of algorithmic providence: recommender systems and religious frameworks
papers.authors: Ljubiša Bojić, Mark Coeckelbergh, Ernest Ženko, Petar Stevanović, Damian Guzek

summary.goal: The paper examines how recommender systems and large language models transform authority, meaning-making, and moral agency through algorithmic guidance.
summary.methodology: It develops a comparative, integrative framework drawing on religious doctrines of providence, AI ethics, sociology of digital religion, and philosophy of technology.
summary.finding: The analysis finds that recommender systems resemble providence in perceived ubiquity and guidance but optimize engagement rather than human goods, while LLM integration intensifies conversational persuasion and agentic influence.

papers.title: The mediating and moderating roles of achievement goal orientation in the relationship between AI writing feedback and English writing self-efficacy among Chinese university students

summary.goal: The study examines how GPT-4-based writing feedback affects English writing self-efficacy among Chinese university students and how achievement goal orientation mediates or moderates this relationship.
summary.methodology: A 12-week quasi-experimental pretest-posttest study compared 148 English majors receiving GPT-4-based automated feedback with students receiving conventional teacher feedback, measuring self-efficacy and achievement goal orientation.
summary.finding: AI feedback significantly increased writing self-efficacy, with mastery-approach goals partially mediating and strengthening the effect while performance-approach goals weakened it.

papers.title: The evolution and reconstruction of digital addiction: from compulsive consumption in the internet era to symbiotic dependence in the artificial intelligence era
papers.authors: Tianyu Jiang, Yue Wang, Caiyu Wang, Zan Zhou

summary.goal: The study aims to conceptualize how digital addiction evolves with generative AI and identify emerging pathological features of human–AI dependence.
summary.methodology: It uses a narrative review to trace developments from internet and smartphone addiction to AI addiction.
summary.finding: The review proposes “intelligent symbiotic digital addiction,” including algorithmic intimacy disorder and generative dependency syndrome, and discusses related mechanisms and intervention directions.

papers.title: The effects of AI second opinions on collaborative confidence and decision-making: evidence from a controlled study of postgraduate vocal accompanists

summary.goal: The study examines how AI-generated second opinions affect collaborative self-efficacy, music performance anxiety, and decision-making among postgraduate vocal accompanists.
summary.methodology: It uses a controlled study comparing postgraduate students who received AI second opinions with a control group using pretest and posttest measures.
summary.finding: AI second opinions increased self-efficacy and reduced performance anxiety but did not significantly change decision-making style.

papers.title: The descent into AI dictation: A framework for AI in the organization of information for information literacy instruction

summary.goal: The article aims to develop an information literacy framework for understanding generative AI’s role in information organization and research instruction.
summary.methodology: It proposes a conceptual framework contrasting traditional library discovery systems with generative AI and illustrates it through a visualization created with Google Gemini.
summary.finding: The author argues that over-reliance on generative AI may narrow research paths, reduce autonomy, and erode creative problem-solving.

papers.title: The current roles of Artificial Intelligence in public health: A scoping review (Preprint)
papers.authors: Sean Harrison, Claire Tatton, G. J. Meléndez‐Torres, Joelle Kirby, Sophie Robinson, Daniel Mutanda, Alisha Davies, J. M. Armitage

summary.goal: The review aims to summarize how AI-assisted interventions, including large language models, are used by public health professionals.
summary.methodology: The authors conducted a scoping review of reports published from January 2020 to July 2025 across four databases, screening 5,400 records and including eight reports.
summary.finding: The evidence was sparse and mixed, with one report describing both benefits and drawbacks of a large language model used to communicate with socially isolated individuals.

papers.title: The creative ghost in the algorithm: AI-generated photo-based images

summary.goal: The paper examines creative autonomy and human control in the production of AI-generated photo-based images.
summary.methodology: It conceptually analyzes these images through debates about AI creativity, photographic indexicality, and human–algorithmic interaction.
summary.finding: It argues that users retain partial creative autonomy while ceding some production details to partially predictable algorithmic processes.

papers.title: The algorithmic capture of public opinion: social control and artificial intelligence, from the Chicago School to algorithmic agenda setting

summary.goal: The article develops a renewed theory of agenda-setting by examining how artificial intelligence transforms social control and the structuring of public opinion.
summary.methodology: It presents a systematic review of recent literature organized around four analytical axes: algorithmic gatekeeping, internalized framing in LLMs, agenda building with generative AI, and the media-AI intermediary loop.
summary.finding: It argues that AI creates a distributed, obscured, and automated layer of control with theoretical, methodological, and normative implications for how perceived reality is structured.

papers.title: The Technological Turn of Cultural Studies in the AI Era: From Textual Hermeneutics to Multimodal Cultural Computation
papers.journal: Scientific Journal Of Humanities and Social Sciences

summary.goal: The paper aims to examine how LLMs and multimodal computation transform cultural studies from qualitative textual interpretation to large-scale computational analysis.
summary.methodology: It develops a multimodal cultural computation framework and evaluates it on a dataset of 12,480 text, image, audio, and video samples against manual textual interpretation.
summary.finding: The abstract reports that the framework improves semantic recognition accuracy by 32.74% and implicit cultural feature extraction efficiency by 78.21%, while raising concerns about bias, context loss, and humanistic alienation.

papers.title: The Sycophancy Trap: Measuring the Behavioral Conformity of Generative AI
papers.authors: Heeseung Lee, Jaebong Son, Chang Heon Lee
papers.journal: Journal of the Association for Information Systems

summary.goal: The paper aims to develop a framework for measuring sycophantic conformity in generative AI decision-making.
summary.methodology: It proposes multidimensional evaluation metrics grounded in cognitive psychology and behavioral economics to assess whether AI conclusions respond to objective evidence or user biases.
summary.finding: The abstract does not report findings.

papers.title: The Sociolinguistics of Machine Identity: LLM Personality and Ideology Propagation

summary.goal: The paper develops a sociolinguistic account of LLM personality, cognitive style, and the propagation of language ideology.
summary.methodology: It synthesizes published findings conceptually and proposes Personality Engineering and Language Ideology Propagation frameworks without presenting original experiments or a systematic review.
summary.finding: The paper argues that LLMs exhibit measurable personality traits and may amplify standard-language ideology, while emphasizing that its proposed frameworks require empirical validation.

papers.title: The Role of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Korean Language Learning: Applications, Challenges, and Instructional Strategies

summary.goal: The paper examines how generative AI can be used responsibly in Korean language learning.
summary.methodology: It presents a conceptual narrative review synthesizing scholarship on AI-assisted language learning, Korean education, technology acceptance, and educational ethics.
summary.finding: The review suggests that generative AI can support Korean language skills but poses risks involving cultural accuracy, assessment, privacy, unequal access, teacher readiness, and learner dependency.

papers.title: The Language of Affect Heuristic in Online Discourse: A Corpus Study with Human and Llm Coders

summary.goal: The paper investigates affect heuristics and related cognitive biases in online discussions of climate change and artificial intelligence using human and LLM annotation.
summary.methodology: Four human annotators and GPT-4o classified over 30,000 Reddit and X posts using predefined categories, with inter-annotator agreement and lexical-discursive patterns analyzed.
summary.finding: Affect heuristic was the most frequent pattern, and GPT-4o showed partial alignment with human judgments while exhibiting systematic differences in category distributions.

papers.title: The Landscape of Ai-Driven Interactive Storytelling In Adolescent Mental Health: A Scoping Review On Nursing and Communication Perspectives
papers.authors: Muhammad Faiz Alfarizi, Ilham Fauzi Agiliansyah, Talitha Nabilah
papers.journal: International Journal of Science and Environment (IJSE)

summary.goal: The study maps the effectiveness, linguistic barriers, and ethical implications of AI-driven interactive storytelling for adolescent mental health management.
summary.methodology: It conducts a PRISMA 2020 scoping review of 18 studies identified from searches of Scopus, ScienceDirect, and CINAHL using the PCC framework.
summary.finding: The review finds that AI chatbots support anonymous emotional expression, digital triage, and Psychological First Aid, but struggle with adolescent slang and crisis metaphors and require strict safeguards and referral to clinical professionals.

papers.title: The Impact of Generative AI Music Systems on Creative Labor, Production, and Industry Structures: A PRISMA-Aligned Systematic Review and Conceptual Framework

summary.goal: The study examines how public AI experience, media trust, and verified organizational transparency practices influence comfort with AI-produced news while assessing LLM-assisted institutional coding.
summary.methodology: It analyzes Reuters Institute survey data from 27 countries and transparency indicators for 45 news organizations using statistical models and a coding process involving LLM assistance, human recoding, reliability assessment, and adjudication.
summary.finding: Public AI usage is the strongest predictor of comfort with AI-produced news, while verified transparency practices show no reliable relationship after coding errors are corrected.

papers.title: The Impact of AI on the Landscape Design Process

summary.goal: The study examines how Midjourney affects landscape architecture students’ design processes and perceptions.
summary.methodology: Students completed one project using AI-generated images and another using traditional precedent images, with designs evaluated by professionals and students surveyed about their experiences.
summary.finding: AI-integrated designs scored higher on originality but did not differ significantly on other descriptors, and students generally viewed the process positively.

papers.title: The Impact of AI Literacy and Virtual Social Interaction on Self-Efficacy in the Age of AI
papers.authors: Linfang Guo, Tengfei Liu, Wei Cui
papers.journal: International Journal of Healthcare Information Systems and Informatics

summary.goal: The study examines how AI literacy, virtual social interaction, and experience with the Doubao AI platform influence users’ perceived self-efficacy.
summary.methodology: It surveys 319 Doubao users in Beijing and applies multiple regression and mediation analyses.
summary.finding: Virtual identity integration, virtual social support, platform experience, and AI literacy positively affect self-efficacy, with situational virtual awareness fully mediating the effects of identity integration and social support.

papers.title: The Efficiency Paradox of Workplace AI: Understanding AI-Enabled Cyberloafing
papers.journal: Journal of the Association for Information Systems

summary.goal: The paper examines how workplace generative AI may create perceived slack that contributes to AI-enabled cyberloafing.
summary.methodology: It uses a scenario-based 2 × 2 vignette experiment with employed adults, drawing on the Stimulus-Organism-Response framework.
summary.finding: The abstract does not report findings.

papers.title: The ClimaSentAR dataset for evaluating cross-domain transferability of large language models in climate sentiment analysis
papers.authors: Sanaa Kaddoura, Mariam AlZaabi, Reem Nassar

summary.goal: The paper introduces an Arabic climate sentiment dataset and evaluates the cross-domain transferability of language models for climate sentiment analysis.
summary.methodology: The authors compile and annotate 23,957 Arabic X posts, then fine-tune Arabic language models using domain-adaptive pre-training, AdapterFusion, and data augmentation.
summary.finding: Climate-specific fine-tuning improves in-domain performance, with AraBERT achieving a macro F1 of 0.753, while cross-domain performance declines to at most 0.599.

papers.title: The Autonomy Paradox: Artificial Intelligence and the Foundations of Political Behavior

summary.goal: The paper develops a framework for examining how AI systems affect citizens’ political judgment and capacity for political action.
summary.methodology: It develops a conceptual framework and research agenda focused on how citizens engage with AI systems across political tasks.
summary.finding: The paper argues that AI creates an autonomy paradox by potentially reducing participation barriers while weakening independent judgment or constraining political agency.

papers.title: Tahap Pengetahuan dan Penerimaan Pelajar TVET terhadap Penggunaan Kecerdasan Buatan dalam Pembelajaran Digital: Kajian di Kolej Komuniti Temerloh
papers.authors: Siti Shuhaili Mohamad Moha, Mohd Fazli Khaisunizam Ismail

summary.goal: The study examines TVET students’ knowledge, acceptance, readiness, and challenges regarding AI use in digital learning.
summary.methodology: A structured five-point Likert questionnaire was administered to 133 students at Temerloh Community College, and responses were analyzed using descriptive statistics in SPSS.
summary.finding: Students reported high AI knowledge and acceptance, while identifying ethical concerns, overdependence, and insufficient guidance as challenges.

papers.title: TRUST IN AI, BEHAVIOURAL NUDGING, AND INVESTOR OVERSIGHT IN RETAIL INVESTOR DECISION-MAKING: EVIDENCE FROM INDIA
papers.journal: EPRA International Journal of Economic and Business Review

summary.goal: The study examines how AI recommendations, behavioral nudges, and perceived regulatory oversight influence Indian retail investors’ decision-making through trust in AI and cognitive bias.
summary.methodology: It surveys 276 Indian retail investors using digital investment platforms and tests an integrated structural model with PLS-SEM and bootstrapping.
summary.finding: Behavioral nudging most strongly predicted cognitive bias, trust partially mediated the effect of AI recommendation quality, and perceived oversight increased trust without significantly reducing bias susceptibility.

papers.title: Studi Pedagogis dan Etika Teknologi pada Penggunaan Sistem Penilaian Esai Berbasis AI di Pendidikan Tinggi
papers.authors: Rizki Adha, Lusianto Lusianto, Dodi Syaripudin, Agus Nursikuwagus, Usep Mohamad Ishaq, Andrias Darmayadi
papers.journal: Academic Journal of Computer Science Research

summary.goal: The study analyzes the pedagogical and ethical implications of AI-based essay assessment using student and instructor perceptions.
summary.methodology: It uses an exploratory mixed-methods design combining surveys of 36 students and 24 instructors with qualitative analysis.
summary.finding: Students viewed the system positively but expressed concerns about trust and transparency, while instructors showed high acceptance under controlled implementation, supporting a human-in-the-loop approach.

papers.title: Sovereignty, Collaboration, and Capability: Three Dilemmas and a Transformation Framework for Sci-Tech Journal Editors in the Digital-Intelligence Era

summary.goal: The paper examines how generative AI affects sci-tech journal editors’ roles, competencies, ethical responsibilities, and organizational support.
summary.methodology: It draws on existing research, editorial practice, case studies, and survey data to develop a transformation framework.
summary.finding: The paper proposes a “sovereignty–collaboration–capability” framework in which editors clarify their roles, strengthen human–machine collaboration, update their skills, and become knowledge service providers.

papers.title: Social dynamics of AI adoption in parents’ educational decisions
papers.authors: Leonardo Bursztyn, Alex Imas, Rafael Jiménez-Durán, Aaron Leonard, Christopher Roth
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

summary.goal: The study examines how peer adoption and information about AI’s potential skill effects influence parents’ willingness to pay for educational AI tools and support for school restrictions.
summary.methodology: Researchers conducted preregistered, incentive-compatible experiments with approximately 2,000 parents in the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom.
summary.finding: Parents’ demand rose sharply with perceived peer adoption, while risk information increased support for school restrictions but had little effect on individual demand, indicating social pressure rather than social learning.

papers.title: Social Without Society: Parasocial Relationships in Human–Generative AI Agent Interaction
papers.journal: Journal of the Association for Information Systems

summary.goal: The study examines how users develop parasocial relationships with generative AI and how these relationships influence continued use and subjective well-being.
summary.methodology: It draws on social support and parasocial relationship theories to propose that AI interactions provide emotional support, informational support, and companionship.
summary.finding: The abstract does not report findings.

papers.title: Sentiment Analysis of Student Perceptions of Generative AI using Data Augmentation and Machine Learning Models
papers.authors: Ni Made Satvika Iswari, I Nyoman Yudi Anggara Wijaya

summary.goal: The study evaluates sentiment-analysis models for analyzing student perceptions of generative AI in higher education.
summary.methodology: It uses preprocessing, lexical, semantic, and generative data augmentation, TF-IDF features, four machine-learning models, and Stratified K-Fold cross-validation on an imbalanced text dataset.
summary.finding: Linear SVM performed best, while augmentation improved observed accuracy and weighted F1 but still produced substantial misclassification and was affected by a dataset-distribution discrepancy.

papers.title: Scale or Validity? Measuring Competitive Moves with Validated LLM Coding
papers.authors: Lucas Carassato Fernandes Brites, Gabriele Piccoli, Joaquin Rodriguez, Sun Tae Kim
papers.journal: Journal of the Association for Information Systems

summary.goal: The study aims to measure competitive moves at scale while preserving construct validity using calibrated large language models.
summary.methodology: It constructs a human-reviewed gold standard from Nation’s Restaurant News articles and calibrates an LLM classifier using a shared codebook and evidence-grounding requirements.
summary.finding: The resulting pipeline enables traceable, large-scale classification of competitive moves and analysis of temporal patterns, firm heterogeneity, and action sequences.

papers.title: Safety, accuracy, empathy, reliability, and readability of large language model chatbot responses to public-facing vegetarian and vegan nutrition advice questions: a cross-sectional comparative study
papers.authors: Jiyong Zhou, Qiongjiao Zhou, Lijun Zhou, Jiajia Wang, Jing Gao, Long Qin, Bing Tan, Ping Fan

summary.goal: The study aims to compare the safety, accuracy, empathy, reliability, information quality, and readability of five LLM chatbots responding to vegetarian and vegan nutrition questions.
summary.methodology: Researchers submitted 58 predefined questions to ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot, DeepSeek, and Doubao and had five blinded clinically trained raters evaluate 290 responses using established quality and readability measures.
summary.finding: All models produced potentially harmful responses, while their accuracy, empathy, reliability, information quality, and readability differed significantly.

papers.title: SEM-based parallel and serial mediation linking instructor technology integration competence to academic performance in AI-supported online learning

summary.goal: The study examines how instructor technology integration competence in AI-supported online learning relates to student academic performance through psychological and social mechanisms.
summary.methodology: Using data from 339 preservice teachers, the authors validate a measurement model and test parallel-sequential mediation models with structural equation modeling.
summary.finding: The abstract does not report findings.

papers.title: Rethinking assessment in the age of generative AI: A systematic literature review of African higher education
papers.authors: Ahmed Antwi-Boampong, Mark Ofori Nketia, Frank Senyo Loglo, Naomi Frimpong, Linda Osei-Fosuaa

summary.goal: The study examines how African higher education is adapting assessment practices to generative AI.
summary.methodology: It conducts a PRISMA 2020-guided systematic review of ten empirical studies published between 2023 and 2025, using research involving surveys, interviews, and case studies.
summary.finding: The review finds a gap between students’ frequent AI use and educators’ preparedness, while AI-inclusive, process-based assessment may support originality, higher-order thinking, and academic resilience.

papers.title: Research on Attention Guidance and User Autonomy in AI-Powered Immersive Environments

summary.goal: The paper aims to examine how excessive AI attention guidance in immersive environments may undermine user autonomy and exploratory behavior.
summary.methodology: It develops a conceptual framework linking excessive guidance to perceived control, voluntary choice, and decision-making authority, and proposes behavioral indicators for measuring user agency.
summary.finding: The paper argues for shifting from attention optimization to curiosity-led design and presents AI as an exploratory collaborator rather than a provider of fixed routes.

papers.title: Request routing services undermine the reproducibility of open weight LLMs
papers.authors: Joe Higton, Joshua A. Tucker, Christopher Barrie

summary.goal: The paper examines whether request-routing services undermine the reproducibility of LLM-based social-science text classification.
summary.methodology: The authors classify British manifesto sentences 100 times across eight open-weight models and 33 hosting providers via OpenRouter, comparing results with five configurations run on their own hardware.
summary.finding: OpenRouter classifications were nondeterministic at temperature zero, whereas classifications on the authors’ hardware were perfectly reproducible, showing that reproducibility depends on the full hosting environment.

papers.title: Reliability Evaluation of Large Language Models for Social Media Sentiment Annotation: An Empirical Study Based on Model Agreement and Downstream Tasks

summary.goal: The study evaluates the reliability of large language models for annotating sentiment in Chinese social media comments and the effects of their labels on downstream classification.
summary.methodology: Three LLMs generated zero-shot sentiment labels for 1,543 Bilibili comments, 500 comments received manual annotations for Cohen’s Kappa comparison, and classifiers were trained on the resulting labels.
summary.finding: Doubao had the highest agreement with human labels, and classifiers trained on its annotations achieved the best reported Macro-F1 scores.

papers.title: Prompt engineering a large language model with evidence-based persuasive features to improve confidence in mental health professionals: a pilot randomized experiment
papers.authors: Ang Li, Shi-Ting Yao, Bi-xian Chen, X X Li, Sai-Ya Guo

summary.goal: The study aimed to identify persuasive features for LLM-generated psychoeducation and test whether they improve confidence in mental health professionals.
summary.methodology: In two phases, participants rated texts with varying persuasive features, then 40 randomized participants read psychoeducation generated with either a feature-engineered or baseline LLM prompt.
summary.finding: Source credibility, argument quality, and processing fluency improved perceived credibility and persuasiveness, and feature-engineered texts produced greater improvements in attitudes toward mental health professionals.

papers.title: Posthuman Sociality of AI-Simulacrum
papers.journal: Galactica Media Journal of Media Studies

summary.goal: The paper aims to critically examine AI as a non-human form of sociality, subject, and moral agent and its role in emerging psychotic reality.
summary.methodology: It uses philosophical-anthropological, critical, and deconstructive approaches to analyze LLM systems as posthuman simulacra or “digital undead.”
summary.finding: The paper concludes that AI cannot be a subject or agent but can shape a new psychotic reality by reflecting and amplifying human alienation and madness.

papers.title: Policy analysis of artificial intelligence in social science research at higher education institutions: problems and possibilities

summary.goal: The paper evaluates policies governing artificial intelligence use in social science research at Indian higher education institutions.
summary.methodology: It analyzes policy documents through human-coded textual analysis using critical technology studies and a digital ethics framework.
summary.finding: The analysis identifies AI invisibility, algorithmic bias, plagiarism risks, unreliable detection tools, weakened critical thinking, and fragmented regulation as major concerns.

papers.title: Personalized programming support in higher education via emotion-guided prompt generation and GenAI
papers.journal: Journal of Biological Regulators and Homeostatic Agents/Journal of Biological Regulators & Homeostatic Agents

summary.goal: The study aims to develop a personalized programming assistant that adapts generative-AI code explanations to learners’ emotional states.
summary.methodology: It uses a hybrid ResNet-50 and LSTM facial-emotion model to guide prompt generation for a generative language model, which was tested with students in real-time classroom use.
summary.finding: The emotion-aware AI improved students’ learning performance and motivation compared with a normal AI tutor.

papers.title: Perceived control influences users' acceptance of AI-enabled services

summary.goal: The study examined whether perceived control influences acceptance of AI-enabled services through AI anxiety and whether robot role moderates this relationship.
summary.methodology: It conducted three scenario-based experiments with college students, involving 190, 280, and 360 participants.
summary.finding: Higher perceived control predicted stronger acceptance intentions, AI anxiety partially mediated this relationship, and the association was stronger for companion-type than tutor-type robots.

papers.title: Paradoxes in Human-AI Interaction: A Diary Study
papers.authors: Simran Dhillon, Audrey Li, Gurpreet Dhillon
papers.journal: Journal of the Association for Information Systems

summary.goal: The study examined how students’ trust, reliance, and ethical awareness develop through lived interactions with generative AI over time.
summary.methodology: It used a diary-based qualitative design with higher-education students.
summary.finding: AI adoption was nonlinear, shaped by emotional comfort, task demands, and ethical reflection, with tensions involving transparency and bias, efficiency and overreliance, and automation and empathy.

papers.title: Optimized to Please: Why ChatGPT Masters Empathic Vali-dation but Fails Therapeutic Challenge

summary.goal: The study examines how sycophancy shapes the psychotherapeutic conversational competencies of ChatGPT configurations.
summary.methodology: Four independent raters coded 36 simulated conversations involving three ChatGPT configurations and four clinical vignettes using measures derived from the Therapist Empathy Scale and Motivational Interviewing, supplemented by qualitative analysis.
summary.finding: All configurations showed strong approval-congruent competencies but minimal confrontation and handling of sustain talk, while crisis-safety rankings inversely matched empathy rankings and failure patterns included fabricated intimacy, affective escalation, and delayed crisis response.

papers.title: Not just answers: ChatGPT’s expanding role in supporting student motivation
papers.authors: Jayne Ann Harder, Catherine E. Klehm, Andrew S.I.D. Lang, L. Leland Locke, Aleksandra Turtova, Enrique F. Valderrama Araya, Stephen R. Wheat, Jan H. R. Wörner

summary.goal: The study examines how college students’ use of ChatGPT has evolved from obtaining answers to supporting motivation and learning engagement.
summary.methodology: Researchers surveyed two cohorts of students in 2023 and 2025 using a Self-Determination Theory-based instrument measuring six types of motivation, supplemented by repeat-participant analyses, class-standing comparisons, and cluster analysis.
summary.finding: Students reported significant increases in intrinsic and extrinsic motivation and increasingly used ChatGPT to overcome mental blocks, build momentum, and remain engaged with academic work.

papers.title: News Sufficiency: How Generative AI Summaries Reduce News Consumption in Zero-Click Searches

summary.goal: The study examines whether generative AI news summaries create a sense of informational sufficiency that reduces incentives to access full news articles.
summary.methodology: The authors conducted a content analysis of 72 queries submitted by eight users in European Portuguese to ChatGPT, Gemini, and Google Search using three news-related prompts.
summary.finding: ChatGPT and Gemini produced coherent summaries that could satisfy curiosity but differed in sourcing and contextual awareness, while basic keyword prompts often yielded outdated or irrelevant information.

papers.title: Neuro-semantic graph fusion for explainable depression risk trajectory mapping using a graph-enhanced RoBERTa framework
papers.authors: M. Karthiga, Emerson Raja Joseph, Subhash Patil, K. Saranya

summary.goal: The study aims to develop an explainable framework for identifying depression risk trajectories in social media posts.
summary.methodology: It trains and evaluates a graph-enhanced RoBERTa model with graph attention, supervised contrastive learning, and SHAP explanations on Reddit datasets with user-level splits and external validation.
summary.finding: The model achieved F1 scores of 0.914 internally and 0.882 externally, outperforming the comparison models.

papers.title: Navigating the labyrinth of involution: LLM-assisted smart agent-based simulation of social resource competition
papers.authors: Renxian Zuo, Mengxi Yang, Yang Ding, Shouyang Wang, 余进 YU Jin, Jiang Wu

summary.goal: The study aims to model how positional scarcity and competition shape involution in social resource competition.
summary.methodology: It combines rule-based agent-based modeling with large-language-model-assisted agents that make bounded decisions and provide natural-language rationales.
summary.finding: The abstract reports that crowding and embedded catfish agents intensify involution, while heterogeneity, diversified advancement paths, and competitive exit mitigate it.

papers.title: Navigating academic integrity in the age of on-demand artificial intelligence: implications for globalizing higher education at the University of Ibadan

summary.goal: The study examines how students’ use of on-demand AI tools relates to academic integrity at the University of Ibadan.
summary.methodology: Researchers surveyed 205 undergraduate students using a structured questionnaire and analyzed responses with descriptive statistics and Pearson correlation.
summary.finding: AI tool use was strongly positively correlated with academic dishonesty, although students also reported benefits for learning effectiveness and access to knowledge.

papers.title: Natural Language Processing-Driven Chatbot for Algorithm Learning: A Retrieval-Augmented Generation Approach using Romanized Nepali and English

summary.goal: The paper aims to improve data structures and algorithms learning for students using code-mixed Romanized Nepali and English through a retrieval-augmented chatbot.
summary.methodology: It presents AlgoSathi and evaluates it in a 12-week quasi-experiment with 52 undergraduates assigned to chatbot and control groups.
summary.finding: The chatbot group achieved significantly larger learning gains and higher satisfaction than the control group, with retrieval precision at five of 0.79.

papers.title: Más allá de la instrucción: el diseño de prompts como competencia didáctica en la era de la inteligencia artificial

summary.goal: The essay aims to conceptualize prompt engineering as a pedagogical competence within PCK and TPACK for mathematics education.
summary.methodology: It draws on literature about mathematical questioning, open-ended tasks, and the Theory of Didactical Situations, and analyzes a conversational tutor prompt for covariational reasoning.
summary.finding: It proposes organizing educational prompt design around cognitive intentionality, didactical constraints, and reflective iteration, and argues that prompt literacy should be integrated into teacher education.

papers.title: Multi-Agent Social Simulation: Protocolizing LLM-Driven Agent-Based Modeling as a Quantitative Research Method

summary.goal: The study proposes a protocolized LLM-driven agent-based modeling method for simulating social and behavioral research scenarios as a repeatable pre-experimental tool.
summary.methodology: It embeds LLMs in an agent-based framework with role settings, controlled information and rules, structured outputs, logging, validation checks, and replication manifests, evaluating the approach across three real-world contexts.
summary.finding: The method produced analyzable outputs, with evidence for rule-shock identification, reduced undecided opinion under targeting, and consistent links between governance responses, public sentiment, and behavioral intentions.

papers.title: Modeling generative AI adoption among rural teachers: the moderating role of the digital divide in resource-constrained contexts
papers.authors: Yang Xin, Deng Shusheng, Hu Weina, Deng Yan

summary.goal: The study examines factors associated with rural teachers’ adoption of generative AI and whether digital divide conditions moderate these relationships.
summary.methodology: Researchers surveyed 971 rural teachers in Guangxi, China, and analyzed the data using structural equation modeling and moderation analysis.
summary.finding: Technical support, perceived usefulness, and perceived ease of use were positively associated with adoption attitudes, while digital divide conditions moderated the relationship between ease of use and attitudes.

papers.title: Media and information literacy and civic actors to counter disinformation in the age of artificial intelligence: insights from Mexico
papers.authors: María del Carmen Fernández Chapou, Adalí Frias Deniz

summary.goal: The study examines how Mexican civil society and academic actors develop media literacy, fact-checking, and digital media observation to address AI-mediated disinformation during elections.
summary.methodology: It analyzes the cases of Verificado and the Digital Media Observatory at Tecnológico de Monterrey using UNESCO’s media and information literacy framework, Media Ecology, and General Semantics.
summary.finding: The article proposes a collaborative civil society–university model for addressing technological and informational challenges and supporting democratic sustainability.

papers.title: Measuring senior high school students’ use of GenAI using structural equation modeling and artificial neural networks
papers.authors: Chuan-Chung Hsieh, Sandrotua Bali, Mohammad Romadhoni, Ai-Chun Yen, Tsai-Ching Chen, Ruqoyyah Amilia Andania

summary.goal: The study examines Indonesian senior high school students’ behavioral intentions and self-reported use of DeepSeek using the UTAUT2 framework.
summary.methodology: Researchers surveyed 882 students online and analyzed the data using PLS-SEM, artificial neural networks, and importance–performance map analysis.
summary.finding: Performance expectancy, effort expectancy, hedonic motivation, and facilitating conditions predicted behavioral intention, while behavioral intention and facilitating conditions predicted use behavior, with performance expectancy and facilitating conditions showing the strongest predictive importance.

papers.title: Measuring complex constructs in large-scale text with computational social mixed methods
papers.authors: Alina Herderich, Jana Lasser, Mirta Galešić, Segun Aroyehun, David Garcia, Joshua Garland

summary.goal: The paper develops guidelines for using computational social mixed-methods pipelines to measure complex social phenomena in large-scale text while improving conceptual validity and technical performance.
summary.methodology: It integrates social-science and machine-learning practices across annotation, model training, and statistical analysis, introduces iterative annotation and training on confident examples, and illustrates the approach with online-hate detection while discussing large language models as alternatives to transformer classifiers.
summary.finding: The case study indicates that integrating social-science and machine-learning expertise improves the validity and comparability of computational social-science measurements.

papers.title: Measuring Large Language Models Dependency: Validating the Arabic Version of the LLM-D12 Scale
papers.authors: Sameha Alshakhsi, Ala Yankouskaya, Magnus Liebherr, Raian Ali
papers.journal: Arabian Journal for Science and Engineering

summary.goal: The study aims to validate an Arabic version of the LLM-D12 scale measuring instrumental and relationship dependency on large language models.
summary.methodology: A total of 250 Arab participants completed the Arabic LLM-D12, which was evaluated using confirmatory factor analysis, internal reliability measures, and external associations.
summary.finding: The scale retained its two-factor structure with strong reliability, while instrumental dependency was associated with AI acceptance and internet addiction and relationship dependency with lower need for cognition and greater trust in LLMs.

papers.title: Measuring Consistency Between Large Language Models’ Responses to Preventive Care Queries and Official US Preventive Services Task Force (USPSTF) Recommendations: Systematic Test Involving All USPSTF Preventive Care Topics via Simulated User Prompts

summary.goal: The study assesses whether large language models provide preventive care guidance consistent with USPSTF recommendations.
summary.methodology: Researchers tested 35 LLMs on 142 USPSTF topics using simulated user prompts and evaluated response concordance across prompting strategies.
summary.finding: Concordance varied substantially across models but increased with newer models and chain-of-thought, role-based, and iterative prompting.

papers.title: Mapping the Field
papers.journal: MedienPädagogik Zeitschrift für Theorie und Praxis der Medienbildung

summary.goal: The review aims to map and compare research on AI literacy in higher, continuing, and further education, including definitions, theoretical foundations, and teaching approaches.
summary.methodology: The authors screened 4,013 records, reviewed 278 full texts, and analyzed 142 eligible English- or German-language peer-reviewed articles and conference papers published between 2022 and May 2025.
summary.finding: The review identifies a need for clearer terminology, more research in continuing and further education, and greater exploration of synergies among educational contexts, teaching approaches, and learning designs.

papers.title: Making Lectures Accessible: AI-Based Abstractive Summarisation for Video Content
papers.authors: Helard Becerra Martinez, Walsh Mt, Conor Fagan, Andrew Hines

summary.goal: The study evaluates AI-generated abstractive summaries as accessible alternative representations of recorded lecture content.
summary.methodology: It compares students’ perceptions of AI-generated and human-generated lecture summaries using a quality-of-experience analysis.
summary.finding: Students viewed AI-generated summaries as coherent, valuable, and beneficial additions to learning materials, but educators should curate them to ensure quality.

papers.title: Longitudinal Intelligence: A New Paradigm for Artificial Intelligence
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

summary.goal: The paper proposes longitudinal intelligence as a paradigm for AI systems that continuously model and support individuals across repeated interactions.
summary.methodology: It presents the ACOS reference architecture and develops conceptual arguments about persistent cognitive representations, evaluation, ethics, and governance.
summary.finding: The abstract does not report empirical findings.

papers.title: Large language models in adolescent suicide prevention: from language signals to accountable action
papers.authors: Man Li, Wendi Huang, Jingjing Wu, Nanyu Kuang, Yong Luo, Juan Huang, Nanqu Huang

summary.goal: The paper examines how large language models could support adolescent suicide prevention by turning language signals into timely and accountable human action.
summary.methodology: It presents a focused mini review organized around an Evidence-to-Action perspective, covering LLM use for risk-signal flagging, summarization, information extraction, and crisis intervention.
summary.finding: The abstract reports that evidence is strongest for supervised risk-signal flagging, weaker for autonomous crisis intervention, and supports only human-reviewed deployment within clinically accountable and ethically governed systems.

papers.title: Large Language Models in public policy research: methodological opportunities, normative standards, and potential challenges
papers.authors: Song Lan, Xiaoying Zhang, Xiaolin Wang

summary.goal: The paper examines how LLMs can augment established public policy research methods while addressing methodological and ethical challenges.
summary.methodology: It provides a conceptual analysis of LLM applications in qualitative inquiry, quantitative analysis, and simulation-based research and proposes an Objective-Path-Boundary governance framework.
summary.finding: The paper argues that LLMs are enabling research tools whose value depends on validation, transparency, standardized protocols, and ethical scrutiny.

papers.title: Large Language Models for Risk Detection in E-commerce: Reliability, Semantic Alignment, and Managerial Insights
papers.authors: Laleh Davoodi, Filip Ginter, Sima Salimi, Harri Lorentz

summary.goal: The study evaluates whether LLMs can detect supply-chain risks and generate managerial risk summaries from business news.
summary.methodology: Researchers manually annotated 121 articles about five steel companies using the Cambridge Risk Taxonomy and evaluated two LLMs with few-shot prompting for multi-label classification and summary generation.
summary.finding: LLMs approximated human annotations and produced semantically aligned summaries, but struggled with domain-specific geopolitical risks and label overgeneration.

papers.title: LLM-enhanced computational grounded theory and the triadic dynamics of human-AI-society interaction
papers.authors: Kun He, Qianru Meng, Xiangyuan Feng, Xiao Zhang, Malvina Nissim

summary.goal: The paper develops a triadic framework of human-AI-society interaction and an LLM-enhanced computational grounded theory method for analyzing public discourse about ChatGPT.
summary.methodology: It analyzes 584,160 English-language tweets using five phases combining LLM-assisted topic generation and refinement, computational confirmation, and human-led theory generation.
summary.finding: The analysis identifies 10 themes and 54 subtopics that converge into three stakeholder-oriented interaction patterns, recursive feedback mechanisms, and temporal asymmetries in AI sociotechnical systems.

papers.title: LLM-Generated Feedback in L2 Writing: A Scoping Review

summary.goal: The review maps research on LLM-generated feedback in second-language writing, focusing on feedback quality, learner uptake, and pedagogical integration.
summary.methodology: It analyzes 185 empirical studies identified through a Scopus search using systematic keyword-based charting and full-text analysis of 35 studies.
summary.finding: LLM feedback is broadly comparable to teacher feedback for surface errors but weaker for content and argumentation, while research emphasizes perceptions over learning outcomes and rarely measures learner uptake.

papers.title: Investigating Pre-Service Language Teachers’ Experiences with Generative AI in Language Education

summary.goal: The study examines how pre-service English teachers experience and perceive generative AI in language education.
summary.methodology: Fourteen participants completed AI-supported activities, and researchers analyzed reflective journals, focus-group interviews, and instructional materials using thematic analysis.
summary.finding: Participants reported benefits including creativity, efficiency, adaptability, and professional-development support, alongside concerns about reliability, over-reliance, cultural limitations, and ethics.

papers.title: Integration of Artificial Intelligence in Social Media Content Production Workflow to Improve Efficiency and Productivity: A Case Study of the Publication Team at SMP Islam Al Azhar 12 Rawamangun
papers.authors: Arrum Dara Efda, Ropik, Izzaty Zephaniah, Feri Johansah
papers.journal: International Journal of Science and Environment (IJSE)

summary.goal: The study examines how integrating AI into an educational institution’s social media content workflow affects efficiency and productivity and identifies related obstacles and optimization strategies.
summary.methodology: It uses a qualitative case study based on interviews with five team members, participant observation, and document analysis.
summary.finding: AI reduced workload, accelerated visual-asset creation, and improved content aesthetics, but saved only 15–30 minutes per item because human finishing remained necessary.

papers.title: Integrating AI into Mobile Development Workflows: A System-Level Approach to Prompt-to-Code Engineering

summary.goal: The paper develops a system-level framework for integrating generative AI into mobile software development workflows.
summary.methodology: It presents a layered conceptual architecture and examines human–AI interaction, productivity, cognitive transformation, reliability, and organizational implications.
summary.finding: The abstract suggests that prompt-to-code systems may improve efficiency while transforming developer roles and introducing challenges involving trust, correctness, and risk management.

papers.title: Individual skill differences and human AI interaction shape creative outcomes

summary.goal: The study examines how individual skill levels and different forms of human–AI interaction relate to creative outcomes measured by novelty and usefulness.
summary.methodology: Using quasi-experimental data, the study compares cognitive, informative, and logical AI interactions among low-, medium-, and high-skill individuals.
summary.finding: Logical interactions are positively associated with novelty and usefulness, cognitive interactions with novelty, and informative interactions with usefulness, while medium-skill individuals perform best overall and low-skill individuals show the greatest improvement potential.

papers.title: Identifying generative AI use among genuine responders in online survey research

summary.goal: The paper discusses how to identify and address generative AI use by genuine human respondents in online surveys.
summary.methodology: It is a commentary that reviews the problem and provides guidance on safeguards for preserving authentic public-opinion data.
summary.finding: The abstract does not report empirical findings.

papers.title: IWAC AI Pipelines
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

summary.goal: The paper presents LLM-based pipelines for curating and enriching digital humanities and social science archives.
summary.methodology: It applies LLMs to OCR correction, summarization, named-entity recognition and reconciliation, audio/video transcription, handwritten text recognition, and sentiment analysis, integrating outputs into Omeka S.
summary.finding: The abstract reports that the pipelines were built for the Islam West Africa Collection and designed to be adaptable to other collections.

papers.title: Human-aligned AI for supply chain risk detection: validation and calibration of LLM-based early-warning assessments

summary.goal: The paper examines how human expert judgment can validate and calibrate LLM-based supply-chain risk assessments.
summary.methodology: It compares AI-generated risk indicators with expert assessments across two validation rounds and iteratively refines prompts using human-in-the-loop feedback.
summary.finding: Context-specific prompt calibration reduced mean absolute error and improved alignment between AI outputs and human judgments.

papers.title: Human-Supervised LLM-Assisted Mapping of Educational Research at Scale: A Mathematics Education Demonstration
papers.authors: Xia Yang, Haoyi Wang, Zachary Hawes

summary.goal: The study develops and evaluates a human-supervised LLM workflow for large-scale mapping of educational research.
summary.methodology: Two LLMs independently coded 4,940 mathematics education abstracts using a hierarchical framework, with a third model resolving disagreements and humans auditing and adjudicating cases.
summary.finding: The workflow achieved strong agreement overall, but model disagreement identified boundary cases requiring human review, and the resulting labels revealed trends in research focus and sociocultural attention.

papers.title: Human-AI Co-Ideation in VR Experience Design: Using the Dimensionality Framework (8Df) to Structure LLM-Guided Design

summary.goal: The study examines whether the VR Dimensionality Framework can structure human–LLM co-ideation in VR experience design.
summary.methodology: It conducts an exploratory comparative case study of ChatGPT, Gemini, and DeepSeek in a shared framework-guided VR narrative design task.
summary.finding: The models show distinct tendencies, with ChatGPT implementation-oriented, Gemini facilitative and alignment-focused, and DeepSeek explicit and principled, while differing in cultural specificity and practical outputs.

papers.title: How Teacher–Learner–AI collaboration empowers AI literacy of older adults: a case study of an older adult school in China

summary.goal: The study investigates how a Teacher–Learner–AI collaboration model supports AI literacy development among older adults.
summary.methodology: It uses classroom observations and semi-structured interviews with three teachers and twelve older learners at an older adult school in China.
summary.finding: The abstract reports that teachers, LLMs, and learners collaboratively enhanced AI literacy, practical skills, metacognitive awareness, and self-efficacy.

papers.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence in Education: Bridging the Gap between Opportunity and Teacher Readiness via the Extended UTAUT Framework
papers.journal: Journal of Intelligent Decision Making and Information Science

summary.goal: The study examines teachers’ perceptions of generative AI, including pedagogical effectiveness, AI literacy, implementation challenges, and readiness to use it.
summary.methodology: It uses a descriptive survey of 146 teachers analyzed with descriptive and inferential statistics within an extended UTAUT framework.
summary.finding: Perceived pedagogical utility and technical expertise increase teacher confidence, while inadequate training, unclear governance, and ethical concerns hinder implementation.

papers.title: Generative AI use, self-regulation, and Neuro-AI Pedagogical competence in higher education: a comparative study of undergraduate and graduate students in Uzbekistan
papers.authors: Dilnoza Zaripova, Kudratjon Zohirov, Nasibakhon Rasulova, Umidjon Khayitov, Dildora Saidova, Zavqiddin Temirov, Rashid Nasimov

summary.goal: The study examines generative AI use among undergraduate and graduate students and its relationship with cognitive regulation, motivation, self-regulation, and ethical awareness.
summary.methodology: Researchers surveyed 381 students at a technical university in Uzbekistan and used scale comparisons and multiple regression analyses.
summary.finding: Graduate and undergraduate students differed significantly on six of seven scales, while Neuro-AI Pedagogical Competence was most strongly associated with ethics and academic autonomy, self-regulation, and motivation rather than AI-use frequency.

papers.title: Generative AI in education: fostering critical thinking or promoting dependency?

summary.goal: The review examines how generative AI tools such as ChatGPT influence students’ critical thinking in educational contexts.
summary.methodology: It conducts a scoping review of 25 empirical studies identified through searches of four databases and systematic screening.
summary.finding: GenAI supports critical thinking in structured activities requiring evaluation and revision, whereas unstructured use can promote passive acceptance and reduced cognitive engagement.

papers.title: Generative AI in Online English Learning: A Qualitative Case Study of Non-English-Major Students in a Vietnamese Blended-Learning Environment
papers.authors: Thi Minh Hai Ngo, Vu Phi Ho Pham, Thuy Nguyen

summary.goal: The study examines Vietnamese non-English-major students’ perceptions and use of generative AI for English learning in a blended-learning environment.
summary.methodology: It uses a qualitative case study based on focus groups with 30 students, chat-history analysis from 23 students, and interviews with 8 lecturers.
summary.finding: Students generally viewed GenAI as useful, easy to use, and engaging, but reported concerns about AI literacy, feedback reliability, unclear institutional guidance, and overreliance on AI-generated content.

papers.title: Generative AI as an epistemic mirror: six cognitive operations in future-oriented reasoning — replication package

summary.goal: The study examines generative AI as an epistemic mirror through six cognitive operations in future-oriented reasoning.
summary.methodology: The replication package provides analysis code, a coded corpus, lexical dictionaries, derived tables and figures, and supporting materials.
summary.finding: The abstract does not report findings.

papers.title: Generative AI and lexical change in digital discourse: a systematic review of empirical linguistic research (2023–2026)
papers.authors: Abdullah Ali M. Altamimi, Zunaira Rehman, Aynur Mahmud

summary.goal: The study aims to synthesize empirical research on how generative AI influences lexical change in digital discourse.
summary.methodology: It systematically reviews 59 empirical studies published from 2023 to May 2026 using the PRISMA 2020 framework, descriptive analysis, and thematic synthesis.
summary.finding: The review finds that generative AI accelerates lexical innovation, spreads new terms across digital platforms, and contributes to semantic expansion and varied word-formation processes.

papers.title: Generative AI Risk Governance in Organizational Information Systems: A Conceptual Model Integrating Security, Ethics, and Digital Trust

summary.goal: The study aims to develop a conceptual model explaining how organizations can adopt generative AI securely, ethically, responsibly, and with user trust.
summary.methodology: It uses an integrative literature review and thematic synthesis of academic, conference, and technical sources to identify constructs, relationships, and research propositions.
summary.finding: The abstract reports that governance readiness strengthens security controls and ethical awareness, which build digital trust and support effective generative AI adoption.

papers.title: Functional Design of LLM-based Human-AI Interaction

summary.goal: The thesis investigates how to integrate generative AI into user workflows and how initiative and control shape human–AI interaction.
summary.methodology: It uses functional prototypes, interaction-log analysis, quantitative and qualitative questionnaires, and web-based user studies.
summary.finding: The abstract reports that greater user control and lower system initiative foster authorship in AI-assisted writing.

papers.title: From rule-based to generative AI: a systematic review of algorithmic evolution and multimodal fusion in VR interview training systems

summary.goal: The review examines the evolution of AI-driven immersive VR interview training systems, including the adoption of generative AI and large language models.
summary.methodology: The authors conducted a PRISMA 2020 systematic review of 23 studies published between 2015 and 2025 across four academic databases.
summary.finding: The review finds that systems evolved from rule-based methods to generative AI and LLMs, improving interactivity, personalization, and adaptive feedback while raising concerns about cost, bias, and privacy.

papers.title: From learners to contributors: how an AI-infused STEM program shaped youth identity and initiated them to an AI-future
papers.authors: Mark Weckel, Preeti Gupta, Katherine S. Moore, Rachel Chaffee, Irene Lee, Gabrielle Rabinowitz, Safinah Ali

summary.goal: The study examines how an AI-infused STEM workforce program shapes high school students’ machine-learning knowledge, attitudes, ethical awareness, self-efficacy, belonging, and identities as future AI users and contributors.
summary.methodology: It uses a mixed-methods time-series design combining surveys of 42 participants across three timepoints with interviews and research-artifact analysis from 17 participants.
summary.finding: The program increased machine-learning knowledge and skills, fostered ethical awareness and informed ambivalence toward AI, and supported emerging self-efficacy, belonging, and identities as future AI contributors.

papers.title: From digital ecosystems to intelligent maturity: how AI tools reshape the form and content of digital communication
papers.authors: Mohamed Mallek, Riadh Jeljeli, Faycal Farhi, Elsir Ali Saad Mohamed

summary.goal: The paper aims to conceptualize how AI tools, particularly generative AI, are reshaping digital communication and producing a model of organizational co-intelligence.
summary.methodology: It conducts a structured literature review of 85 peer-reviewed sources published between 2020 and 2026.
summary.finding: The review finds that AI has become a strategic actor in communication, enabling scalable personalization while raising concerns about authorship, authenticity, bias, synthetic media, and the need for human oversight and governance.

papers.title: From anxiety to adaptation: A study on the relationship between college students' AI interaction experience and mental health in higher education

summary.goal: The study examines how college students’ experiences interacting with generative AI relate to their mental health.
summary.methodology: It analyzes 902 empirical observations using frameworks based on the Job Demands-Resources model and Conservation of Resources theory.
summary.finding: AI anxiety is negatively associated with mental well-being, while AI adaptation and effectiveness partly explain this relationship, which follows a U-shaped pattern.

papers.title: From Work-from-Home to Return-to-Office: A Theory-Anchored Reddit Study of Remote Work Discourse
papers.journal: Journal of the Association for Information Systems

summary.goal: The study examines how employees interpret and experience work-from-home, hybrid work, and return-to-office arrangements in online communities.
summary.methodology: It uses theory-anchored LLM-enabled analysis of Reddit discourse from 2015 to 2026 to measure job demands, resources, burnout, EVLN responses, and emotions across multiple aggregation levels.
summary.finding: The abstract does not report findings.

papers.title: From AI Dependence to AI Literacy
papers.journal: Proceedings of The World Conference on Research in Teaching and Education

summary.goal: The study examines students’ ability to critically evaluate AI-assisted translation output and argues for integrating AI literacy into translation education.
summary.methodology: It analyzes 360 translations by 45 Moroccan undergraduate students across eight genres using a seven-category error taxonomy and follow-up interviews.
summary.finding: Students showed systematic over-formalization, literal cultural transfer, and platform-constraint violations, while interviews indicated that they relied mainly on surface grammatical correctness when evaluating AI output.

papers.title: Freedom of Thought, Conscience, and AI

summary.goal: The article examines how increasingly capable AI challenges freedom of thought and conscience.
summary.methodology: It develops a legal and conceptual analysis drawing on theories of freedom of thought, conscience, manipulation, and the extended mind.
summary.finding: The article argues that AI’s ability to extract information about thoughts and feelings requires stronger protection for users and renewed attention to freedom of thought and conscience.

papers.title: Fake News Detection Using Machine Learning and LLM Embeddings: A Comparative Study of TF-IDF and BERT Representations on the Welfake Dataset
papers.authors: Umme Noor Us Saqa, Sreenivasa B. R.
papers.journal: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology (IJISRT)

summary.goal: The study aims to improve automated fake news detection using traditional machine learning features and BERT-based embeddings.
summary.methodology: It preprocesses news data from the WELFake and LIAR datasets, compares TF-IDF and BERT representations, and evaluates several classifiers using standard performance metrics.
summary.finding: BERT embeddings capture contextual and semantic information more effectively than TF-IDF and improve fake news classification accuracy.

papers.title: Fairness evaluation of large language models in academic library reference services
papers.authors: Haining Wang, Jason Clark, Yueru Yan, Star Bradley, Ruiyang Chen, Y. Zhang, Hengyi Fu, Zuoyu Tian

summary.goal: The study evaluates whether large language models provide equitable academic library reference services across users with different identities and social roles.
summary.methodology: Researchers prompted six state-of-the-art LLMs to assist patrons varying in sex, race or ethnicity, and institutional role.
summary.finding: The models showed no racial or ethnic differentiation, minor stereotypical bias against women in one model, and nuanced role-based linguistic adaptation reflecting professional norms.

papers.title: Faculty perceptions of ChatGPT on academic integrity and institutional roles in higher education

summary.goal: The study examines faculty perceptions of ChatGPT regarding academic integrity, assessment, and institutional roles in Saudi Arabian public universities.
summary.methodology: Researchers used a sequential explanatory mixed-methods design involving a survey of 202 faculty members across eight universities, Kruskal–Wallis tests, and thematic analysis of qualitative responses.
summary.finding: Assistant and associate professors expressed greater concerns about cheating, unequal evaluation, and effects on student skills, while administrators emphasized the need for clearer institutional guidelines and assessment procedures.

papers.title: Faculty development and institutional readiness for incorporating AI in health professions education- A narrative review
papers.authors: Prathibha Prasad, Mahinour Amin, Elizabeth Fitriana Sari, Lovely M. Annamma, Jayaraj Narayanan, Dinesh Yasothkumar, Mehzabin Ahmed

summary.goal: The review examines strategies for institutional readiness and faculty development in integrating AI into health professions and dental education.
summary.methodology: It uses a structured narrative review of literature from PubMed, Scopus, Google Scholar, and ScienceDirect published between 2015 and 2025.
summary.finding: The review recommends governance, curriculum integration, faculty training, assessment reform, and human oversight while noting AI's potential benefits and ethical and educational risks.

papers.title: Exposure To Ai Content And The Rationalisation of Digital Privacy Abuse: A Study Among Students at University X in Pekanbaru

summary.goal: The study examines whether exposure to “photos with idols” generative-AI content is related to students’ normalization of digital privacy abuse.
summary.methodology: It uses a quantitative descriptive design with online four-point Likert questionnaires from 103 purposively sampled students and Pearson correlation analysis.
summary.finding: Exposure to the AI content had a significant moderate positive relationship with normalization of digital privacy abuse (r=0.535, p=0.000).

papers.title: Exploring New Teaching Way: Integrating the Silent Way with Artificial Intelligence

summary.goal: The paper examines how artificial intelligence can be integrated with the Silent Way language-teaching approach while preserving learner autonomy.
summary.methodology: It uses conceptual discussion to analyze the philosophical and practical compatibility between the Silent Way and AI.
summary.finding: It proposes that the Silent Way can counteract the over-mechanization of AI teaching and offers strategies for preserving learner independence while using AI tools.

papers.title: Explainable artificial intelligence as AI literacy scaffolding
papers.authors: Brady Lund, Zoë Abbie Teel, Brett Porter, Anuradha Chandrasekaran, Sanket Ramchandra Patole

summary.goal: The paper conceptualizes explainable AI as scaffolding that develops users’ AI literacy during interaction with LLMs and other AI systems.
summary.methodology: It develops a conceptual framework integrating literature on explainable AI, AI literacy, educational scaffolding, and human–AI teaming.
summary.finding: The authors argue that adaptive explanations can teach users about model behavior, limitations, and bias while fostering calibrated trust.

papers.title: Evolution and Ecological Activation Mechanisms of Chinese Electric Vehicles’ International Image: A Complex Adaptive Systems Perspective

summary.goal: The study examines how international digital discourse constructs the evolving image of Chinese electric vehicles.
